ko.title: [소비자 심리학 #13] "4,000명이 구매함"이 당신에게 통하는 이유 (그렇지 않아야 한다는 걸 알면서도)

segments.src: > We rarely shop alone: the people we belong to, the people we admire, and even total strangers' reviews quietly shape what we buy.
segments.tr: > 우리는 혼자 쇼핑하는 경우는 드뭅니다. 우리가 속한 집단, 동경하는 집단, 심지어 완전히 모르는 사람들의 리뷰까지도 우리의 구매 품목을 조용히 결정합니다.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: Picture two taco trucks parked side by side.
segments.tr: 나란히 주차된 두 대의 타코 트럭을 상상해 보세요.

segments.src: One has a line of 15 people.
segments.tr: 한쪽에는 15명이 줄을 서 있습니다.

segments.src: The other has nobody.
segments.tr: 다른 쪽에는 아무도 없습니다.

segments.src: Most of us join the line, even though it means waiting longer.
segments.tr: 우리 대부분은 더 오래 기다려야 함에도 불구하고 줄에 합류합니다.

segments.src: We don't know anything about the food yet, but other people's choices feel like information.
segments.tr: 아직 음식에 대해 아무것도 모르지만, 다른 사람들의 선택이 정보처럼 느껴지기 때문입니다.

segments.src: That is **social influence**: our buying decisions change because of what other people do, say, or think.
segments.tr: 이것이 바로 **사회적 영향(social influence)**입니다. 다른 사람들이 행동하고, 말하고, 생각하는 것에 따라 우리의 구매 결정이 달라지는 현상입니다.

segments.src: Consumer psychologists usually split it into three connected ideas.
segments.tr: 소비자 심리학자들은 대개 이를 서로 연결된 세 가지 개념으로 나눕니다.

segments.src: Reference groups.** These are the groups we use as a yardstick for our own choices.
segments.tr: 준거 집단(Reference groups).** 이는 우리 자신의 선택을 위한 척도로 사용하는 집단입니다.

segments.src: They come in a few types:
segments.tr: 이들은 몇 가지 유형으로 나뉩니다.

segments.src: - **Membership groups**: groups you already belong to, like your coworkers, your family, or your running club.
segments.tr: - **소속 집단(Membership groups)**: 동료, 가족, 러닝 클럽처럼 이미 자신이 속해 있는 집단.

segments.src: - **Aspirational groups**: groups you'd like to belong to, like the senior engineers you hope to join or athletes you look up to.
segments.tr: - **동경 집단(Aspirational groups)**: 함께하고 싶은 시니어 엔지니어들이나 우러러보는 운동선수들처럼 속하고 싶은 집단.

segments.src: - **Dissociative groups**: groups you *don't* want to be associated with. People sometimes avoid a brand because "that's not who I am."
segments.tr: - **회피 집단(Dissociative groups)**: 관련되고 *싶지 않은* 집단. 사람들은 "저건 내 모습이 아니야"라며 특정 브랜드를 피하기도 합니다.

segments.src: Reference groups matter most for products other people can see, like sneakers, cars, phones, and the bag you carry to work.
segments.tr: 준거 집단은 스니커즈, 자동차, 휴대전화, 출근길에 드는 가방처럼 다른 사람이 볼 수 있는 제품에 가장 중요하게 작용합니다.

segments.src: They matter much less for things nobody notices, like your brand of dish soap.
segments.tr: 주방 세제 브랜드처럼 아무도 알아차리지 못하는 것에는 훨씬 덜 중요합니다.

segments.src: Word of mouth (WOM).** This means consumers telling other consumers about products.
segments.tr: 구전(Word of mouth, WOM).** 이는 소비자들이 서로에게 제품에 대해 이야기하는 것을 의미합니다.

segments.src: Today that includes a friend's text ("you have to try this"), a TikTok review, and a Reddit thread.
segments.tr: 오늘날에는 친구의 문자 메시지("이거 꼭 써봐"), 틱톡 리뷰, 레딧 스레드 등이 이에 포함됩니다.

segments.src: People tend to trust WOM more than ads because the speaker doesn't seem to be trying to sell anything.
segments.tr: 말하는 사람이 무언가를 팔려고 하는 것처럼 보이지 않기 때문에, 사람들은 광고보다 구전을 더 신뢰하는 경향이 있습니다.

segments.src: That trust is also why undisclosed paid endorsements are a problem.
segments.tr: 이러한 신뢰 때문에 출처를 밝히지 않은 유료 광고(뒷광고)가 문제가 되는 것입니다.

segments.src: The U.S.
segments.tr: 미국

segments.src: Federal Trade Commission requires influencers to disclose material connections to brands.
segments.tr: 연방거래위원회(FTC)는 인플루언서들에게 브랜드와의 경제적 이해관계 공개를 요구합니다.

segments.src: Social proof.** This term was popularized by psychologist Robert Cialdini.
segments.tr: 사회적 증거(Social proof).** 이 용어는 심리학자 로버트 치알디니에 의해 대중화되었습니다.

segments.src: When we're unsure what to do, we look at what others are doing and assume they know something.
segments.tr: 무엇을 해야 할지 확신이 없을 때, 우리는 다른 사람들이 하는 것을 보고 그들이 무언가를 알고 있다고 가정합니다.

segments.src: Uncertainty makes the effect stronger, and so does similarity: the more the "others" resemble us, the more their choices count.
segments.tr: 불확실할수록 이 효과는 더 강해지며, 유사성도 영향을 미칩니다. 즉, "다른 사람들"이 우리와 닮을수록 그들의 선택이 더 큰 비중을 차지합니다.

segments.src: Classic research shows how strong this pull is.
segments.tr: 고전적인 연구들은 이 끌림이 얼마나 강한지 보여줍니다.

segments.src: In Solomon Asch's 1950s line-judgment experiments, many participants went along at least once with a group answer that was plainly wrong.
segments.tr: 솔로몬 애쉬의 1950년대 선분 판단 실험에서, 많은 참가자가 명백히 틀린 집단 답변에 적어도 한 번 이상 동조했습니다.

segments.src: Some of that was because they doubted their own eyes.
segments.tr: 그 이유 중 일부는 자신의 눈을 의심했기 때문입니다.

segments.src: Some was because they didn't want to stand out.
segments.tr: 일부는 튀고 싶지 않았기 때문입니다.

segments.src: Psychologists call these two motives:
segments.tr: 심리학자들은 이 두 가지 동기를 다음과 같이 부릅니다.

segments.src: - **Informational influence**: "They probably know better."
segments.tr: - **정보적 영향(Informational influence)**: "저 사람들이 아마 더 잘 알 거야."

segments.src: - **Normative influence**: "I want to fit in."
segments.tr: - **규범적 영향(Normative influence)**: "무리에 섞이고 싶어."

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 일상생활 속에서

segments.src: You're on Amazon looking for a $30 pair of wireless earbuds.
segments.tr: 아마존에서 30달러짜리 무선 이어폰을 찾고 있습니다.

segments.src: Two options look almost the same:
segments.tr: 두 가지 옵션이 거의 똑같아 보입니다.

segments.src: - **Option A**: 4.4 stars, 12,000+ ratings, a "#1 Best Seller" badge, and "2K+ bought in past month"
segments.tr: - **옵션 A**: 별점 4.4개, 12,000개 이상의 평가, "#1 베스트셀러" 배지, "지난달 2천 개 이상 구매됨"

segments.src: - **Option B**: 4.6 stars, 38 ratings
segments.tr: - **옵션 B**: 별점 4.6개, 평가 38개

segments.src: On paper, B is rated higher, yet many shoppers pick A anyway.
segments.tr: 이론상으로는 B의 평점이 더 높지만, 많은 쇼핑객은 결국 A를 선택합니다.

segments.src: Each part of the listing is doing a different job:
segments.tr: 목록의 각 부분은 서로 다른 역할을 하고 있습니다.

segments.src: - **Social proof:** The rating count and the "bought in past month" line tell you that lots of people chose A. When you can't test earbuds yourself, volume feels safer than a slightly higher average from a few people.
segments.tr: - **사회적 증거:** 평가 횟수와 "지난달 구매됨" 문구는 수많은 사람이 A를 선택했음을 알려줍니다. 이어폰을 직접 테스트해 볼 수 없을 때, 소수의 약간 더 높은 평균 평점보다 판매량이 더 안전하게 느껴집니다.

segments.src: - **Word of mouth:** You scroll to reviews from people "like you," such as "Great for the gym" or "I use these on my commute on the subway." Similar reviewers carry extra weight.
segments.tr: - **구전:** "헬스용으로 최고" 또는 "지하철 출퇴근용으로 씀"과 같이 "나와 비슷한" 사람들의 리뷰로 스크롤을 내립니다. 비슷한 리뷰어들의 의견은 더 큰 무게를 가집니다.

segments.src: - **Reference groups:** If your coworkers all wear AirPods, you might pay $100 more just to match them. Earbuds are visible, so they say something about you.
segments.tr: - **준거 집단:** 동료들이 모두 AirPods를 착용하고 있다면, 그들과 맞추기 위해 100달러를 더 지불할 수도 있습니다. 이어폰은 눈에 잘 띄므로 자신을 드러내는 수단이 되기 때문입니다.

segments.src: Businesses use the same levers on purpose: "Most popular" plan labels on SaaS pricing pages, "Join 50,000 marketers" on newsletter sign-ups, and customer logos on B2B websites.
segments.tr: 기업들도 의도적으로 이러한 레버를 사용합니다. SaaS 가격 페이지의 "가장 인기 있는" 요금제 라벨, 뉴스레터 가입 페이지의 "5만 명의 마케터와 함께하세요", B2B 웹사이트의 고객 로고 등이 그 예입니다.

segments.src: A well-known hotel study found that a card saying *most guests here reuse their towels* got more people to reuse towels than a card about saving the environment.
segments.tr: *이곳의 대다수 투숙객이 수건을 재사용합니다*라는 카드가 환경 보호에 대한 카드보다 더 많은 사람의 수건 재사용을 이끌어냈다는 유명한 호텔 연구 결과가 있습니다.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 3줄 요약

segments.src: 1. Reference groups (the ones you belong to, want to join, or want to avoid) shape choices most strongly for products that other people can see.
segments.tr: 1. 준거 집단(소속되어 있거나, 가입하고 싶거나, 피하고 싶은 집단)은 다른 사람이 볼 수 있는 제품에 대해 선택에 가장 큰 영향을 미칩니다.

segments.src: 2. Word of mouth is persuasive because it seems independent of the seller. That makes honesty and disclosure important.
segments.tr: 2. 구전은 판매자와 무관해 보이기 때문에 설득력이 있습니다. 그렇기 때문에 정직함과 정보 공개가 중요합니다.

segments.src: 3. Social proof is strongest when we feel uncertain and when the "others" seem similar to us. It works through both "they know better" and "I want to fit in."
segments.tr: 3. 사회적 증거는 우리가 불확실함을 느낄 때, 그리고 "다른 사람들"이 우리와 비슷해 보일 때 가장 강력해집니다. 이는 "그들이 더 잘 안다"와 "어울리고 싶다"라는 두 가지 측면을 통해 작동합니다.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 셀프 퀴즈

segments.src: **Q1.** A college student avoids buying a certain car brand because they think "that's what my parents' boring friends drive."
segments.tr: **Q1.** 한 대학생이 "부모님의 지루한 친구들이나 타는 차"라는 생각에 특정 자동차 브랜드 구매를 피합니다.

segments.src: Which type of reference group is at work?
segments.tr: 어떤 유형의 준거 집단이 작용하고 있나요?

segments.src: - (a) Membership group
segments.tr: - (a) 소속 집단

segments.src: - (b) Aspirational group
segments.tr: - (b) 동경 집단

segments.src: - (c) Dissociative group
segments.tr: - (c) 회피 집단

segments.src: (True/False)** Social proof tends to be strongest when a shopper is very confident and already knows exactly what they want.
segments.tr: (참/거짓)** 사회적 증거는 쇼핑객이 매우 자신감에 차 있고 자신이 원하는 바를 정확히 알고 있을 때 가장 강한 경향이 있습니다.

segments.src: **Q3.** A SaaS pricing page puts a "Most Popular" label on its middle plan.
segments.tr: **Q3.** 한 SaaS 가격 책정 페이지가 중간 요금제에 "가장 인기(Most Popular)" 라벨을 붙였습니다.

segments.src: Which principle is it mainly using?
segments.tr: 어느 원리를 주로 활용하고 있는 것인가요?

segments.src: - (a) Social proof
segments.tr: - (a) 사회적 증거

segments.src: - (b) Dissociative influence
segments.tr: - (b) 회피적 영향

segments.src: - (c) Product scarcity
segments.tr: - (c) 제품 희소성

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 오늘의 용어

segments.src: - **Reference group**: Any group a person uses as a standard for their own attitudes and purchases.
segments.tr: - **준거 집단(Reference group)**: 개인이 자신의 태도와 구매에 대한 기준으로 사용하는 모든 집단.

segments.src: - **Aspirational group**: A group you don't belong to yet but would like to join or resemble.
segments.tr: - **동경 집단(Aspirational group)**: 아직 속해 있지 않지만 가입하고 싶거나 닮고 싶은 집단.

segments.src: - **Word of mouth (WOM)**: Consumers sharing information and opinions about products with each other, offline or online.
segments.tr: - **구전(Word of mouth, WOM)**: 소비자들이 오프라인이나 온라인에서 서로 제품에 대한 정보와 의견을 나누는 것.

segments.src: - **Social proof**: The tendency to treat other people's behavior as evidence of the right choice, especially when we're unsure.
segments.tr: - **사회적 증거(Social proof)**: 특히 확신이 없을 때, 다른 사람의 행동을 올바른 선택의 증거로 취급하는 경향.

segments.src: - **Normative vs. informational influence**: Going along to fit in vs. going along because you think others know better.
segments.tr: - **규범적 vs. 정보적 영향(Normative vs. informational influence)**: 무리에 섞이기 위해 동조하는 것 vs. 다른 사람들이 더 잘 안다고 생각해서 동조하는 것.

segments.src: *Answers: Q1 is (c).
segments.tr: *정답: Q1은 (c).

segments.src: The student is steering away from a group they don't want to be identified with.
segments.tr: 학생은 자신이 동일시되기 원하지 않는 집단으로부터 멀어지고 있습니다.

segments.src: Q2 is False.
segments.tr: Q2는 거짓(False).

segments.src: Social proof works best when people feel **uncertain**; confident shoppers rely more on their own judgment.
segments.tr: 사회적 증거는 사람들이 **불확실성**을 느낄 때 가장 잘 작동하며, 자신 있는 쇼핑객은 자신의 판단에 더 의존합니다.

segments.src: Q3 is (a).
segments.tr: Q3은 (a).

segments.src: "Most Popular" tells visitors what others chose and suggests that choosing it is safe and normal.
segments.tr: "가장 인기(Most Popular)"는 방문객에게 다른 사람들이 무엇을 선택했는지 알려주며 그것을 선택하는 것이 안전하고 정상적임을 암시합니다.

segments.src: Scarcity would be something like "Only 3 left."*
segments.tr: 희소성은 "3개 남음" 같은 것일 겁니다.*

zh.title: [Consumer Psychology #13] 为什么“4000人购买”对你管用（即使你知道它不该管用）

segments.src: > We rarely shop alone: the people we belong to, the people we admire, and even total strangers' reviews quietly shape what we buy.
segments.tr: > 我们很少独自购物：我们所属的群体、我们钦佩的人，甚至完全陌生的评价，都在悄悄塑造我们的购买行为。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今天的概念

segments.src: Picture two taco trucks parked side by side.
segments.tr: 想象两辆并排停放的塔可餐车。

segments.src: One has a line of 15 people.
segments.tr: 其中一辆排着15个人的队伍。

segments.src: The other has nobody.
segments.tr: 另一辆空无一人。

segments.src: Most of us join the line, even though it means waiting longer.
segments.tr: 我们大多数人都会加入队伍，尽管这意味着要等更长时间。

segments.src: We don't know anything about the food yet, but other people's choices feel like information.
segments.tr: 我们对食物还一无所知，但别人的选择感觉就像是信息。

segments.src: That is **social influence**: our buying decisions change because of what other people do, say, or think.
segments.tr: 这就是**社会影响**：我们的购买决策因别人的行为、言语或想法而改变。

segments.src: Consumer psychologists usually split it into three connected ideas.
segments.tr: 消费心理学家通常将其分为三个相关联的概念。

segments.src: Reference groups.** These are the groups we use as a yardstick for our own choices.
segments.tr: 参照群体。** 这些是我们用来衡量自己选择的标准群体。

segments.src: They come in a few types:
segments.tr: 它们有几种类型：

segments.src: - **Membership groups**: groups you already belong to, like your coworkers, your family, or your running club.
segments.tr: - **成员群体**：你已经是其中一员的群体，比如你的同事、家人或跑步俱乐部。

segments.src: - **Aspirational groups**: groups you'd like to belong to, like the senior engineers you hope to join or athletes you look up to.
segments.tr: - **抱负群体**：你希望加入的群体，比如你希望加入的高级工程师群体或你崇拜的运动员。

segments.src: - **Dissociative groups**: groups you *don't* want to be associated with. People sometimes avoid a brand because "that's not who I am."
segments.tr: - **脱离群体**：你*不希望*与之产生关联的群体。人们有时会避开某个品牌，因为“那不是我”。

segments.src: Reference groups matter most for products other people can see, like sneakers, cars, phones, and the bag you carry to work.
segments.tr: 对于别人能看到的产品，参照群体最重要，比如运动鞋、汽车、手机和你上班背的包。

segments.src: They matter much less for things nobody notices, like your brand of dish soap.
segments.tr: 对于没人注意的东西，它们就没那么重要了，比如你用的洗洁精品牌。

segments.src: Word of mouth (WOM).** This means consumers telling other consumers about products.
segments.tr: 口碑（WOM）。** 这意味着消费者向其他消费者介绍产品。

segments.src: Today that includes a friend's text ("you have to try this"), a TikTok review, and a Reddit thread.
segments.tr: 如今这包括朋友的发信（“你一定要试试这个”）、TikTok 评测和 Reddit 帖子。

segments.src: People tend to trust WOM more than ads because the speaker doesn't seem to be trying to sell anything.
segments.tr: 人们倾向于比广告更信任口碑，因为说话者似乎并非在试图兜售什么。

segments.src: That trust is also why undisclosed paid endorsements are a problem.
segments.tr: 这种信任也是未披露的有偿背书成为问题的原因。

segments.src: The U.S.
segments.tr: 美国

segments.src: Federal Trade Commission requires influencers to disclose material connections to brands.
segments.tr: 联邦贸易委员会要求网红披露与品牌的实质性联系。

segments.src: Social proof.** This term was popularized by psychologist Robert Cialdini.
segments.tr: 社会认同。** 这个术语由心理学家罗伯特·西奥迪尼推广。

segments.src: When we're unsure what to do, we look at what others are doing and assume they know something.
segments.tr: 当我们不确定该怎么做时，我们会看看别人在做什么，并假设他们知道些什么。

segments.src: Uncertainty makes the effect stronger, and so does similarity: the more the "others" resemble us, the more their choices count.
segments.tr: 不确定性会使这种效应更强，相似性也是如此：“其他人”越像我们，他们的选择就越有分量。

segments.src: Classic research shows how strong this pull is.
segments.tr: 经典研究表明这种拉力有多强。

segments.src: In Solomon Asch's 1950s line-judgment experiments, many participants went along at least once with a group answer that was plainly wrong.
segments.tr: 在所罗门·阿希20世纪50年代的线段判断实验中，许多参与者至少有一次顺从了明显错误的集体答案。

segments.src: Some of that was because they doubted their own eyes.
segments.tr: 其中一部分原因是因为他们怀疑自己的眼睛。

segments.src: Some was because they didn't want to stand out.
segments.tr: 一部分原因是因为他们不想显得与众不同。

segments.src: Psychologists call these two motives:
segments.tr: 心理学家将这两种动机称为：

segments.src: - **Informational influence**: "They probably know better."
segments.tr: - **信息性影响**：“他们可能更了解。”

segments.src: - **Normative influence**: "I want to fit in."
segments.tr: - **规范性影响**：“我想融入其中。”

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 在日常生活中

segments.src: You're on Amazon looking for a $30 pair of wireless earbuds.
segments.tr: 你在亚马逊上寻找一副30美元的无线耳机。

segments.src: Two options look almost the same:
segments.tr: 两个选项看起来几乎一模一样：

segments.src: - **Option A**: 4.4 stars, 12,000+ ratings, a "#1 Best Seller" badge, and "2K+ bought in past month"
segments.tr: - **选项 A**：4.4星，12,000+条评分，“#1 畅销品”徽章，以及“过去一个月售出2千+”

segments.src: - **Option B**: 4.6 stars, 38 ratings
On paper, B is rated higher, yet many shoppers pick A anyway.
segments.tr: 理论上讲，B 的评分更高，但许多购物者还是选择了 A。

segments.src: Each part of the listing is doing a different job:
segments.tr: 列表的每个部分都在发挥不同的作用：

segments.src: - **Social proof:** The rating count and the "bought in past month" line tell you that lots of people chose A. When you can't test earbuds yourself, volume feels safer than a slightly higher average from a few people.
segments.tr: - **社会认同：** 评分数量和“过去一个月售出”一行告诉你，很多人选择了 A。当你无法亲自测试耳机时，销量比少数人给出稍高的平均分感觉更安全。

segments.src: - **Word of mouth:** You scroll to reviews from people "like you," such as "Great for the gym" or "I use these on my commute on the subway." Similar reviewers carry extra weight.
segments.tr: - **口碑：** 你会滚动浏览“像你一样”的人的评价，例如“非常适合健身房”或“我在地铁通勤时用这些”。相似的评论者具有额外的分量。

segments.src: - **Reference groups:** If your coworkers all wear AirPods, you might pay $100 more just to match them. Earbuds are visible, so they say something about you.
segments.tr: - **参照群体：** 如果你的同事都戴 AirPods，你可能会多花100美元只为了和他们匹配。耳机是可见的，因此它们代表了你的一部分。

segments.src: Businesses use the same levers on purpose: "Most popular" plan labels on SaaS pricing pages, "Join 50,000 marketers" on newsletter sign-ups, and customer logos on B2B websites.
segments.tr: 企业刻意使用相同的杠杆：SaaS 定价页面上的“最受欢迎”计划标签、时事通讯注册时的“加入50,000名营销人员”，以及 B2B 网站上的客户徽标。

segments.src: A well-known hotel study found that a card saying *most guests here reuse their towels* got more people to reuse towels than a card about saving the environment.
segments.tr: 一项著名的酒店研究发现，一张写着*这里的绝大多数客人都重复使用毛巾*的卡片，比一张关于节约环境的卡片更能促使人们重复使用毛巾。

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 3行总结

segments.src: 1. Reference groups (the ones you belong to, want to join, or want to avoid) shape choices most strongly for products that other people can see.
segments.tr: 1. 参照群体（你所属的、想加入的或想避开的群体）对别人能看到的产品选择影响最大。

segments.src: 2. Word of mouth is persuasive because it seems independent of the seller. That makes honesty and disclosure important.
segments.tr: 2. 口碑很有说服力，因为它似乎独立于卖家。这使得诚实和披露变得重要。

segments.src: 3. Social proof is strongest when we feel uncertain and when the "others" seem similar to us. It works through both "they know better" and "I want to fit in."
segments.tr: 3. 当我们感到不确定且“其他人”看起来与我们相似时，社会认同最为强烈。它通过“他们更懂”和“我想合群”起作用。

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 自测

segments.src: **Q1.** A college student avoids buying a certain car brand because they think "that's what my parents' boring friends drive."
segments.tr: **Q1.** 一名大学生避免购买某个汽车品牌，因为他们觉得“那是我的父母那些无聊的朋友开的车。”

segments.src: Which type of reference group is at work?
segments.tr: 起作用的是哪种类型的参照群体？

segments.src: - (a) Membership group
segments.tr: - (a) 成员群体

segments.src: - (b) Aspirational group
segments.tr: - (b) 抱负群体

segments.src: - (c) Dissociative group
segments.tr: - (c) 脱离群体

segments.src: (True/False)** Social proof tends to be strongest when a shopper is very confident and already knows exactly what they want.
segments.tr: (对/错)** 当购物者非常自信并且已经确切知道自己想要什么时，社会认同往往最强。

segments.src: **Q3.** A SaaS pricing page puts a "Most Popular" label on its middle plan.
segments.tr: **Q3.** SaaS 定价页面在其中间计划上贴上了“最受欢迎”的标签。

segments.src: Which principle is it mainly using?
segments.tr: 它主要使用的是哪个原则？

segments.src: - (a) Social proof
segments.tr: - (a) 社会认同

segments.src: - (b) Dissociative influence
segments.tr: - (b) 脱离影响

segments.src: - (c) Product scarcity
segments.tr: - (c) 产品稀缺性

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 今天的术语

segments.src: - **Reference group**: Any group a person uses as a standard for their own attitudes and purchases.
segments.tr: - **参照群体**：一个人用作自己态度和购买标准的任何群体。

segments.src: - **Aspirational group**: A group you don't belong to yet but would like to join or resemble.
segments.tr: - **抱负群体**：你尚不属于但希望加入或模仿的群体。

segments.src: - **Word of mouth (WOM)**: Consumers sharing information and opinions about products with each other, offline or online.
segments.tr: - **口碑（WOM）**：消费者在离线或在线相互分享有关产品的信和意见。

segments.src: - **Social proof**: The tendency to treat other people's behavior as evidence of the right choice, especially when we're unsure.
segments.tr: - **社会认同**：将别人的行为视为正确选择证据的倾向，尤其是在我们不确定的时候。

segments.src: - **Normative vs. informational influence**: Going along to fit in vs. going along because you think others know better.
segments.tr: - **规范性与信息性影响**：为了合群而顺从，与因为认为别人更懂而顺从。

segments.src: *Answers: Q1 is (c).
segments.tr: *答案：Q1 是 (c)。

segments.src: The student is steering away from a group they don't want to be identified with.
segments.tr: 这名学生在刻意避开一个他们不想与之产生关联的群体。

segments.src: Q2 is False.
segments.tr: Q2 是错的。

segments.src: Social proof works best when people feel **uncertain**; confident shoppers rely more on their own judgment.
segments.tr: 当人们感到**不确定**时，社会认同效果最好；自信的购物者更多地依靠自己的判断。

segments.src: Q3 is (a).
segments.tr: Q3 是 (a)。

segments.src: "Most Popular" tells visitors what others chose and suggests that choosing it is safe and normal.
segments.tr: “最受欢迎”告诉访客其他人选择了什么，并暗示选择它是安全且正常的。

segments.src: Scarcity would be something like "Only 3 left."*
segments.tr: 稀缺性大概类似于“只剩3个”。*

hi.title: [उपभोक्ता मनोविज्ञान #13] "4,000 लोगों ने यह खरीदा" आप पर असर क्यों करता है (भले ही आप जानते हों कि ऐसा नहीं होना चाहिए)

segments.src: > We rarely shop alone: the people we belong to, the people we admire, and even total strangers' reviews quietly shape what we buy.
segments.tr: > हम शायद ही कभी अकेले खरीदारी करते हैं: जिन समूहों से हम जुड़े होते हैं, जिन लोगों की हम प्रशंसा करते हैं, और यहां तक कि पूरी तरह अजनबियों की समीक्षाएं भी चुपचाप तय करती हैं कि हम क्या खरीदते हैं।

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## आज की अवधारणा

segments.src: Picture two taco trucks parked side by side.
segments.tr: दो टैको ट्रक्स को एक-दूसरे के बगल में खड़े हुए सोचिए।

segments.src: One has a line of 15 people.
segments.tr: एक के सामने 15 लोगों की लाइन है।

segments.src: The other has nobody.
segments.tr: दूसरे के सामने कोई नहीं है।

segments.src: Most of us join the line, even though it means waiting longer.
segments.tr: ज़्यादातर लोग लाइन में लग जाते हैं, भले ही इसका मतलब ज़्यादा इंतज़ार हो।

segments.src: We don't know anything about the food yet, but other people's choices feel like information.
segments.tr: हम अभी खाने के बारे में कुछ नहीं जानते, लेकिन दूसरे लोगों के चुनाव हमें जानकारी जैसे लगते हैं।

segments.src: That is **social influence**: our buying decisions change because of what other people do, say, or think.
segments.tr: यही **सामाजिक प्रभाव** है: हमारे खरीदारी के फैसले इस बात से बदल जाते हैं कि दूसरे लोग क्या करते, कहते या सोचते हैं।

segments.src: Consumer psychologists usually split it into three connected ideas.
segments.tr: उपभोक्ता मनोवैज्ञानिक इसे आम तौर पर तीन आपस में जुड़े विचारों में बांटते हैं।

segments.src: Reference groups.** These are the groups we use as a yardstick for our own choices.
segments.tr: संदर्भ समूह।** ये वे समूह हैं जिन्हें हम अपने चुनावों के पैमाने के रूप में इस्तेमाल करते हैं।

segments.src: They come in a few types:
segments.tr: इनके कुछ प्रकार होते हैं:

segments.src: - **Membership groups**: groups you already belong to, like your coworkers, your family, or your running club.
segments.tr: - **सदस्यता समूह**: वे समूह जिनके आप पहले से सदस्य हैं, जैसे आपके सहकर्मी, आपका परिवार, या आपका रनिंग क्लब।

segments.src: - **Aspirational groups**: groups you'd like to belong to, like the senior engineers you hope to join or athletes you look up to.
segments.tr: - **आकांक्षी समूह**: वे समूह जिनका आप सदस्य बनना चाहेंगे, जैसे वरिष्ठ इंजीनियर जिनके साथ आप जुड़ने की उम्मीद करते हैं, या वे एथलीट जिन्हें आप आदर्श मानते हैं।

segments.src: - **Dissociative groups**: groups you *don't* want to be associated with. People sometimes avoid a brand because "that's not who I am."
segments.tr: - **विच्छेदी समूह**: वे समूह जिनसे आप *जुड़ना नहीं* चाहते। कभी-कभी लोग किसी ब्रांड से इसलिए बचते हैं क्योंकि "वह मेरे जैसा नहीं है।"

segments.src: Reference groups matter most for products other people can see, like sneakers, cars, phones, and the bag you carry to work.
segments.tr: संदर्भ समूह उन उत्पादों के लिए सबसे ज़्यादा मायने रखते हैं जिन्हें दूसरे लोग देख सकते हैं, जैसे स्नीकर्स, कारें, फ़ोन, और वह बैग जो आप ऑफ़िस ले जाते हैं।

segments.src: They matter much less for things nobody notices, like your brand of dish soap.
segments.tr: उन चीज़ों के लिए ये कहीं कम मायने रखते हैं जिन पर किसी का ध्यान नहीं जाता, जैसे आपका डिश सोप का ब्रांड।

segments.src: Word of mouth (WOM).** This means consumers telling other consumers about products.
segments.tr: मुँह-ज़बानी प्रचार (WOM)।** इसका मतलब है उपभोक्ताओं का एक-दूसरे को उत्पादों के बारे में बताना।

segments.src: Today that includes a friend's text ("you have to try this"), a TikTok review, and a Reddit thread.
segments.tr: आज इसमें किसी दोस्त का मैसेज ("तुम्हें यह ज़रूर आज़माना चाहिए"), एक TikTok समीक्षा, और एक Reddit थ्रेड शामिल हैं।

segments.src: People tend to trust WOM more than ads because the speaker doesn't seem to be trying to sell anything.
segments.tr: लोग विज्ञापनों की तुलना में WOM पर ज़्यादा भरोसा करते हैं, क्योंकि बोलने वाला ऐसा नहीं लगता कि वह कुछ बेचने की कोशिश कर रहा है।

segments.src: That trust is also why undisclosed paid endorsements are a problem.
segments.tr: यही भरोसा इस बात को भी समस्या बनाता है कि बिना घोषणा वाले भुगतान किए गए समर्थन (endorsements) गलत हैं।

segments.src: The U.S.
segments.tr: अमेरिका का

segments.src: Federal Trade Commission requires influencers to disclose material connections to brands.
segments.tr: Federal Trade Commission इन्फ़्लुएंसर्स से माँग करता है कि वे ब्रांडों के साथ अपने महत्वपूर्ण संबंधों का खुलासा करें।

segments.src: Social proof.** This term was popularized by psychologist Robert Cialdini.
segments.tr: सामाजिक प्रमाण।** यह शब्द मनोवैज्ञानिक रॉबर्ट सियाल्डिनी ने लोकप्रिय बनाया।

segments.src: When we're unsure what to do, we look at what others are doing and assume they know something.
segments.tr: जब हमें पता नहीं होता कि क्या करना है, तो हम देखते हैं कि दूसरे क्या कर रहे हैं और मान लेते हैं कि वे कुछ जानते हैं।

segments.src: Uncertainty makes the effect stronger, and so does similarity: the more the "others" resemble us, the more their choices count.
segments.tr: अनिश्चितता इस प्रभाव को और मज़बूत बनाती है, और समानता भी: "दूसरे" लोग हमारे जितने ज़्यादा मिलते-जुलते होंगे, उनके चुनाव उतने ही ज़्यादा मायने रखेंगे।

segments.src: Classic research shows how strong this pull is.
segments.tr: क्लासिक शोध दिखाता है कि यह खिंचाव कितना मज़बूत होता है।

segments.src: In Solomon Asch's 1950s line-judgment experiments, many participants went along at least once with a group answer that was plainly wrong.
segments.tr: सॉलोमन ऐश के 1950 के दशक के लाइन-जजमेंट प्रयोगों में, कई प्रतिभागी कम से कम एक बार ऐसे समूह-उत्तर से सहमत हो गए जो साफ़ तौर पर गलत था।

segments.src: Some of that was because they doubted their own eyes.
segments.tr: इसका कुछ कारण यह था कि उन्हें अपनी आँखों पर शक हुआ।

segments.src: Some was because they didn't want to stand out.
segments.tr: कुछ इसलिए था कि वे अलग दिखना नहीं चाहते थे।

segments.src: Psychologists call these two motives:
segments.tr: मनोवैज्ञानिक इन दो प्रेरणाओं को इस तरह कहते हैं:

segments.src: - **Informational influence**: "They probably know better."
segments.tr: - **सूचनात्मक प्रभाव**: "शायद वे बेहतर जानते हैं।"

segments.src: - **Normative influence**: "I want to fit in."
segments.tr: - **मानदंडात्मक प्रभाव**: "मैं घुलना-मिलना चाहता हूँ।"

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## रोज़मर्रा की ज़िंदगी में

segments.src: You're on Amazon looking for a $30 pair of wireless earbuds.
segments.tr: आप Amazon पर $30 वाले वायरलेस ईयरबड्स ढूंढ रहे हैं।

segments.src: Two options look almost the same:
segments.tr: दो विकल्प लगभग एक जैसे दिखते हैं:

segments.src: - **Option A**: 4.4 stars, 12,000+ ratings, a "#1 Best Seller" badge, and "2K+ bought in past month"
segments.tr: - **विकल्प A**: 4.4 स्टार, 12,000+ रेटिंग, "#1 Best Seller" बैज, और "पिछले महीने 2K+ लोगों ने खरीदा"

segments.src: - **Option B**: 4.6 stars, 38 ratings
On paper, B is rated higher, yet many shoppers pick A anyway.
segments.tr: कागज़ पर B की रेटिंग ज़्यादा है, फिर भी कई खरीदार A चुन लेते हैं।

segments.src: Each part of the listing is doing a different job:

es.title: [Psicología del consumidor #13] ¿Por qué «4,000 personas compraron esto» te afecta (aunque sepas que no debería)?

segments.src: > We rarely shop alone: the people we belong to, the people we admire, and even total strangers' reviews quietly shape what we buy.
segments.tr: > Rara vez compramos solos: los grupos a los que pertenecemos, las personas que admiramos e incluso las reseñas de desconocidos influyen discretamente en lo que compramos.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Concepto de hoy

segments.src: Picture two taco trucks parked side by side.
segments.tr: Imagina dos food trucks de tacos estacionados uno al lado del otro.

segments.src: One has a line of 15 people.
segments.tr: Uno tiene una fila de 15 personas.

segments.src: The other has nobody.
segments.tr: El otro no tiene a nadie.

segments.src: Most of us join the line, even though it means waiting longer.
segments.tr: La mayoría nos unimos a la fila, aunque eso signifique esperar más.

segments.src: We don't know anything about the food yet, but other people's choices feel like information.
segments.tr: Todavía no sabemos nada de la comida, pero las decisiones de otras personas nos parecen información.

segments.src: That is **social influence**: our buying decisions change because of what other people do, say, or think.
segments.tr: Eso es la **influencia social**: nuestras decisiones de compra cambian por lo que otras personas hacen, dicen o piensan.

segments.src: Consumer psychologists usually split it into three connected ideas.
segments.tr: Los psicólogos del consumidor suelen dividirla en tres ideas relacionadas.

segments.src: Reference groups.** These are the groups we use as a yardstick for our own choices.
segments.tr: Grupos de referencia.** Son los grupos que usamos como referencia para nuestras propias decisiones.

segments.src: They come in a few types:
segments.tr: Hay varios tipos:

segments.src: - **Membership groups**: groups you already belong to, like your coworkers, your family, or your running club.
segments.tr: - **Grupos de pertenencia**: grupos a los que ya perteneces, como tus compañeros de trabajo, tu familia o tu club de running.

segments.src: - **Aspirational groups**: groups you'd like to belong to, like the senior engineers you hope to join or athletes you look up to.
segments.tr: - **Grupos aspiracionales**: grupos a los que te gustaría pertenecer, como los ingenieros senior a los que esperas unirte o los atletas que admiras.

segments.src: - **Dissociative groups**: groups you *don't* want to be associated with. People sometimes avoid a brand because "that's not who I am."
segments.tr: - **Grupos disociativos**: grupos con los que *no* quieres que te asocien. A veces la gente evita una marca porque «eso no es lo que soy».

segments.src: Reference groups matter most for products other people can see, like sneakers, cars, phones, and the bag you carry to work.
segments.tr: Los grupos de referencia importan más en productos que otros pueden ver, como las zapatillas, los coches, los teléfonos y el bolso que llevas al trabajo.

segments.src: They matter much less for things nobody notices, like your brand of dish soap.
segments.tr: Importan mucho menos en cosas que nadie nota, como la marca de tu detergente para platos.

segments.src: Word of mouth (WOM).** This means consumers telling other consumers about products.
segments.tr: Boca a boca (WOM, por sus siglas en inglés).** Consiste en que los consumidores hablen de productos entre ellos.

segments.src: Today that includes a friend's text ("you have to try this"), a TikTok review, and a Reddit thread.
segments.tr: Hoy incluye el mensaje de un amigo («tienes que probar esto»), una reseña en TikTok y un hilo de Reddit.

segments.src: People tend to trust WOM more than ads because the speaker doesn't seem to be trying to sell anything.
segments.tr: La gente tiende a confiar más en el boca a boca que en los anuncios porque quien habla no parece estar intentando vender nada.

segments.src: That trust is also why undisclosed paid endorsements are a problem.
segments.tr: Esa confianza también es el motivo por el que los respaldos pagados no declarados son un problema.

segments.src: The U.S.
segments.tr: La

segments.src: Federal Trade Commission requires influencers to disclose material connections to brands.
segments.tr: Comisión Federal de Comercio de EE. UU. exige a los influencers declarar las relaciones relevantes con las marcas.

segments.src: Social proof.** This term was popularized by psychologist Robert Cialdini.
segments.tr: Prueba social.** Este término fue popularizado por el psicólogo Robert Cialdini.

segments.src: When we're unsure what to do, we look at what others are doing and assume they know something.
segments.tr: Cuando no sabemos qué hacer, miramos lo que hacen los demás y suponemos que saben algo.

segments.src: Uncertainty makes the effect stronger, and so does similarity: the more the "others" resemble us, the more their choices count.
segments.tr: La incertidumbre hace que el efecto sea más fuerte, y también lo hace la similitud: cuanto más se parecen los «otros» a nosotros, más cuentan sus decisiones.

segments.src: Classic research shows how strong this pull is.
segments.tr: La investigación clásica muestra lo fuerte que es esta atracción.

segments.src: In Solomon Asch's 1950s line-judgment experiments, many participants went along at least once with a group answer that was plainly wrong.
segments.tr: En los experimentos de juicio de líneas de Solomon Asch, en los años cincuenta, muchos participantes se plegaron al menos una vez a una respuesta grupal que era claramente errónea.

segments.src: Some of that was because they doubted their own eyes.
segments.tr: En parte, porque dudaban de lo que veían.

segments.src: Some was because they didn't want to stand out.
segments.tr: En parte, porque no querían destacar.

segments.src: Psychologists call these two motives:
segments.tr: Los psicólogos llaman a estos dos motivos:

segments.src: - **Informational influence**: "They probably know better."
segments.tr: - **Influencia informativa**: «Probablemente ellos saben más».

segments.src: - **Normative influence**: "I want to fit in."
segments.tr: - **Influencia normativa**: «Quiero encajar».

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## En la vida cotidiana

segments.src: You're on Amazon looking for a $30 pair of wireless earbuds.
segments.tr: Estás en Amazon buscando unos auriculares inalámbricos de 30 $.

segments.src: Two options look almost the same:
segments.tr: Dos opciones se ven casi iguales:

segments.src: - **Option A**: 4.4 stars, 12,000+ ratings, a "#1 Best Seller" badge, and "2K+ bought in past month"
segments.tr: - **Opción A**: 4,4 estrellas, más de 12.000 valoraciones, una insignia de «#1 más vendido» y «2K+ comprados el último mes»

segments.src: - **Option B**: 4.6 stars, 38 ratings
segments.tr: - **Opción B**: 4,6 estrellas, 38 valoraciones

segments.src: On paper, B is rated higher, yet many shoppers pick A anyway.
segments.tr: Sobre el papel, la B tiene mejor valoración, pero muchos compradores eligen igualmente la A.

segments.src: Each part of the listing is doing a different job:
segments.tr: Cada parte de la ficha cumple una función distinta:

segments.src: - **Social proof:** The rating count and the "bought in past month" line tell you that lots of people chose A. When you can't test earbuds yourself, volume feels safer than a slightly higher average from a few people.
segments.tr: - **Prueba social:** El número de valoraciones y la línea «comprados el último mes» indican que mucha gente eligió la A. Cuando no puedes probar los auriculares tú mismo, el volumen parece más seguro que una media ligeramente superior basada en pocas personas.

segments.src: - **Word of mouth:** You scroll to reviews from people "like you," such as "Great for the gym" or "I use these on my commute on the subway." Similar reviewers carry extra weight.
segments.tr: - **Boca a boca:** Lees las reseñas de personas «como tú», como «Genial para el gimnasio» o «Los uso en mi trayecto diario en metro». Las reseñas de perfiles similares tienen más peso.

segments.src: - **Reference groups:** If your coworkers all wear AirPods, you might pay $100 more just to match them. Earbuds are visible, so they say something about you.
segments.tr: - **Grupos de referencia:** Si tus compañeros de trabajo usan todos AirPods, podrías pagar 100 $ más solo para igualarlos. Los auriculares son visibles, así que dicen algo sobre ti.

segments.src: Businesses use the same levers on purpose: "Most popular" plan labels on SaaS pricing pages, "Join 50,000 marketers" on newsletter sign-ups, and customer logos on B2B websites.
segments.tr: Las empresas usan las mismas palancas a propósito: etiquetas de «Plan más popular» en las páginas de precios de SaaS, «Únete a 50,000 especialistas en marketing» en los formularios de suscripción a newsletters, y logotipos de clientes en las webs B2B.

segments.src: A well-known hotel study found that a card saying *most guests here reuse their towels* got more people to reuse towels than a card about saving the environment.
segments.tr: Un conocido estudio sobre hoteles encontró que un cartel que decía *la mayoría de los huéspedes de aquí reutilizan sus toallas* conseguía que más personas reutilizaran las toallas que un cartel sobre la protección del medio ambiente.

segments.src: - **Aspirational groups**: groups you'd like to belong to, like the senior engineers you hope to join or athletes you look up to.

segments.src: - **Dissociative groups**: groups you *don't* want to be associated with. People sometimes avoid a brand because "that's not who I am."
segments.tr: - **المجموعات النافرة**: المجموعات التي *لا* تريد أن تُنسب إليها. يتجنب الناس أحيانًا علامة تجارية لأن «هذا ليس أنا».

segments.src: Uncertainty makes the effect stronger, and so does similarity: the more the "others" resemble us, the more their choices count.
segments.tr: يزيد عدم اليقين من قوة هذا التأثير، وكذلك التشابه: فكلما شابهنا «الآخرون» أكثر، زاد وزن اختياراتهم.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## في الحياة اليومية

segments.src: You're on Amazon looking for a $30 pair of wireless earbuds.
segments.tr: أنت على أمازون تبحث عن سماعات لاسلكية بسعر 30 دولارًا.

segments.src: Two options look almost the same:
segments.tr: يبدو الخياران متشابهين تقريبًا:

segments.src: - **Option A**: 4.4 stars, 12,000+ ratings, a "#1 Best Seller" badge, and "2K+ bought in past month"
segments.tr: - **الخيار A**: 4.4 نجمة، وأكثر من 12,000 تقييم، وشارة «الأكثر مبيعًا رقم 1»، و«أكثر من 2K اشتُري خلال الشهر الماضي»

segments.src: - **Option B**: 4.6 stars, 38 ratings
segments.tr: - **الخيار B**: 4.6 نجمة، و38 تقييمًا

segments.src: On paper, B is rated higher, yet many shoppers pick A anyway.
segments.tr: على الورق، يحظى B بتقييم أعلى، ومع ذلك يختار كثير من المتسوقين A.

segments.src: Each part of the listing is doing a different job:
segments.tr: يؤدي كل جزء من الإعلان وظيفة مختلفة:

segments.src: - **Social proof:** The rating count and the "bought in past month" line tell you that lots of people chose A. When you can't test earbuds yourself, volume feels safer than a slightly higher average from a few people.
segments.tr: - **الدليل الاجتماعي:** يخبرك عدد التقييمات وعبارة «اشتُري خلال الشهر الماضي» أن أعدادًا كبيرة من الناس اختارت A. فعندما لا تستطيع تجربة السماعات بنفسك، يبدو الحجم الكبير أكثر أمانًا من متوسط أعلى قليلًا من عدد قليل من الأشخاص.

segments.src: - **Word of mouth:** You scroll to reviews from people "like you," such as "Great for the gym" or "I use these on my commute on the subway." Similar reviewers carry extra weight.
segments.tr: - **التوصية الشفهية:** تمرر إلى مراجعات من أشخاص «مثلك»، مثل «ممتازة للصالة الرياضية» أو «أستخدمها في تنقلي اليومي بالمترو». للمراجعين المشابهين وزن إضافي.

segments.src: - **Reference groups:** If your coworkers all wear AirPods, you might pay $100 more just to match them. Earbuds are visible, so they say something about you.
segments.tr: - **المجموعات المرجعية:** إذا كان زملاؤك جميعًا يرتدون AirPods، فقد تدفع 100 دولار إضافية فقط لتتماشى معهم. السماعات مرئية، لذلك فهي تقول شيئًا عنك.

segments.src: Businesses use the same levers on purpose: "Most popular" plan labels on SaaS pricing pages, "Join 50,000 marketers" on newsletter sign-ups, and customer logos on B2B websites.
segments.tr: تستخدم الشركات الأدوات نفسها عن قصد: وسوم «الأكثر شيوعًا» على خطط صفحات أسعار البرمجيات كخدمة، و«انضم إلى 50,000 مسوّق» في تسجيلات النشرات البريدية، وشعارات العملاء على مواقع الشركات B2B.

segments.tr: وجدت دراسة فندقية معروفة أن بطاقة تقول *معظم النزلاء هنا يعيدون استخدام مناشفهم* دفعت عددًا أكبر من الناس إلى إعادة استخدام المناشف مقارنةً ببطاقة عن توفير البيئة.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## ملخص في ثلاثة أسطر

segments.src: 1. Reference groups (the ones you belong to, want to join, or want to avoid) shape choices most strongly for products that other people can see.
segments.tr: 1. تُشكّل المجموعات المرجعية (التي تنتمي إليها، أو ترغب في الانضمام إليها، أو تريد تجنبها) الاختيارات بقوة أكبر في المنتجات التي يستطيع الآخرون رؤيتها.

segments.src: 2. Word of mouth is persuasive because it seems independent of the seller. That makes honesty and disclosure important.
segments.tr: 2. التوصية الشفهية مقنعة لأنها تبدو مستقلة عن البائع. ولذلك تكتسب الصدق والإفصاح أهمية.

segments.src: 3. Social proof is strongest when we feel uncertain and when the "others" seem similar to us. It works through both "they know better" and "I want to fit in."
segments.tr: 3. يكون الدليل الاجتماعي أقوى ما يكون عندما نشعر بعدم اليقين وعندما يبدو «الآخرون» مشابهين لنا. ويعمل من خلال «هم يعرفون أفضل» و«أريد أن أندمج» معًا.

pt.title: [Psicologia do Consumidor #13] Por que "4,000 pessoas compraram isto" funciona com você (mesmo quando você sabe que não deveria)

segments.src: > We rarely shop alone: the people we belong to, the people we admire, and even total strangers' reviews quietly shape what we buy.
segments.tr: > Raramente compramos sozinhos: as pessoas com quem nos identificamos, as pessoas que admiramos e até as avaliações de desconhecidos moldam discretamente o que compramos.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Conceito de Hoje

segments.src: Picture two taco trucks parked side by side.
segments.tr: Imagine dois food trucks de tacos estacionados lado a lado.

segments.src: One has a line of 15 people.
segments.tr: Um deles tem uma fila de 15 pessoas.

segments.src: The other has nobody.
segments.tr: O outro não tem ninguém.

segments.src: Most of us join the line, even though it means waiting longer.
segments.tr: A maioria de nós entra na fila, mesmo que isso signifique esperar mais.

segments.src: We don't know anything about the food yet, but other people's choices feel like information.
segments.tr: Ainda não sabemos nada sobre a comida, mas as escolhas dos outros parecem uma informação.

segments.src: That is **social influence**: our buying decisions change because of what other people do, say, or think.
segments.tr: Isso é **influência social**: nossas decisões de compra mudam por causa do que outras pessoas fazem, dizem ou pensam.

segments.src: Consumer psychologists usually split it into three connected ideas.
segments.tr: Os psicólogos do consumidor geralmente a dividem em três ideias conectadas.

segments.src: Reference groups.** These are the groups we use as a yardstick for our own choices.
segments.tr: Grupos de referência.** São os grupos que usamos como parâmetro para nossas próprias escolhas.

segments.src: They come in a few types:
segments.tr: Eles aparecem em alguns tipos:

segments.src: - **Membership groups**: groups you already belong to, like your coworkers, your family, or your running club.
segments.tr: - **Grupos de pertencimento**: grupos aos quais você já pertence, como colegas de trabalho, sua família ou seu clube de corrida.

segments.src: - **Aspirational groups**: groups you'd like to belong to, like the senior engineers you hope to join or athletes you look up to.
segments.tr: - **Grupos aspiracionais**: grupos aos quais você gostaria de pertencer, como os engenheiros sêniores que você espera integrar ou os atletas que você admira.

segments.src: - **Dissociative groups**: groups you *don't* want to be associated with. People sometimes avoid a brand because "that's not who I am."
segments.tr: - **Grupos dissociativos**: grupos com os quais você *não* quer ser associado. Às vezes as pessoas evitam uma marca porque "não é a minha cara".

segments.src: Reference groups matter most for products other people can see, like sneakers, cars, phones, and the bag you carry to work.
segments.tr: Grupos de referência importam mais para produtos que outras pessoas podem ver, como tênis, carros, celulares e a bolsa que você leva para o trabalho.

segments.src: They matter much less for things nobody notices, like your brand of dish soap.
segments.tr: Importam bem menos para coisas que ninguém percebe, como a marca do seu detergente de louça.

segments.src: Word of mouth (WOM).** This means consumers telling other consumers about products.
segments.tr: Boca a boca (WOM).** Isso significa consumidores contando a outros consumidores sobre produtos.

segments.src: Today that includes a friend's text ("you have to try this"), a TikTok review, and a Reddit thread.
segments.tr: Hoje, isso inclui a mensagem de um amigo ("você precisa experimentar isto"), uma avaliação no TikTok e um tópico no Reddit.

segments.src: People tend to trust WOM more than ads because the speaker doesn't seem to be trying to sell anything.
segments.tr: As pessoas tendem a confiar mais no boca a boca do que em anúncios, porque quem fala não parece estar tentando vender nada.

segments.src: That trust is also why undisclosed paid endorsements are a problem.
segments.tr: Essa confiança também é o motivo pelo qual endossos pagos não divulgados são um problema.

segments.src: Social proof.** This term was popularized by psychologist Robert Cialdini.
segments.tr: Prova social.** Este termo foi popularizado pelo psicólogo Robert Cialdini.

segments.src: When we're unsure what to do, we look at what others are doing and assume they know something.
segments.tr: Quando não temos certeza do que fazer, olhamos o que os outros estão fazendo e presumimos que eles sabem de algo.

segments.src: Uncertainty makes the effect stronger, and so does similarity: the more the "others" resemble us, the more their choices count.
segments.tr: A incerteza torna o efeito mais forte, e a semelhança também: quanto mais os "outros" se parecem conosco, mais suas escolhas contam.

segments.src: Classic research shows how strong this pull is.
segments.tr: A pesquisa clássica mostra o quanto essa força é grande.

segments.src: - **Dissociative groups**: groups you *don't* want to be associated with. People sometimes avoid a brand because "that's not who I am."
segments.tr: - **Kelompok disosiatif**: kelompok yang *tidak* ingin kita kaitkan dengan diri kita. Orang kadang menghindari suatu merek karena “itu bukan saya”.

segments.src: Reference groups matter most for products other people can see, like sneakers, cars, phones, and the bag you carry to work.
segments.tr: Kelompok referensi paling berpengaruh pada produk yang bisa dilihat orang lain, seperti sepatu kets, mobil, ponsel, dan tas yang dibawa ke kantor.

segments.src: They matter much less for things nobody notices, like your brand of dish soap.
segments.tr: Pengaruhnya jauh lebih kecil pada barang yang tidak terlihat orang, seperti merek sabun cuci piring Anda.

segments.src: Word of mouth (WOM).** This means consumers telling other consumers about products.
segments.tr: Word of mouth (WOM).** Ini berarti konsumen menceritakan produk kepada konsumen lain.

segments.src: Today that includes a friend's text ("you have to try this"), a TikTok review, and a Reddit thread.
segments.tr: Saat ini bentuknya mencakup pesan teks dari teman (“kamu harus coba ini”), ulasan di TikTok, dan utas di Reddit.

segments.src: People tend to trust WOM more than ads because the speaker doesn't seem to be trying to sell anything.
segments.tr: Orang cenderung lebih percaya pada WOM dibanding iklan karena pembicaranya tidak terlihat sedang berusaha menjual sesuatu.

segments.src: That trust is also why undisclosed paid endorsements are a problem.
segments.tr: Kepercayaan itulah yang membuat endorsement berbayar yang tidak diungkapkan menjadi masalah.

segments.src: Social proof.** This term was popularized by psychologist Robert Cialdini.
segments.tr: Bukti sosial.** Istilah ini dipopulerkan oleh psikolog Robert Cialdini.

segments.src: When we're unsure what to do, we look at what others are doing and assume they know something.
segments.tr: Saat kita tidak yakin harus berbuat apa, kita melihat apa yang dilakukan orang lain dan menganggap mereka tahu sesuatu.

segments.src: Uncertainty makes the effect stronger, and so does similarity: the more the "others" resemble us, the more their choices count.
segments.tr: Ketidakpastian memperkuat efek ini, begitu pula kemiripan: semakin “orang lain” itu menyerupai kita, semakin besar pengaruh pilihan mereka.

segments.src: Classic research shows how strong this pull is.
segments.tr: Penelitian klasik menunjukkan betapa kuatnya daya tarik ini.

segments.src: In Solomon Asch's 1950s line-judgment experiments, many participants went along at least once with a group answer that was plainly wrong.
segments.tr: Dalam eksperimen penilaian garis Solomon Asch pada tahun 1950-an, banyak partisipan setidaknya sekali mengikuti jawaban kelompok yang jelas-jelas salah.

segments.src: Some of that was because they doubted their own eyes.
segments.tr: Sebagian karena mereka meragukan penglihatan mereka sendiri.

segments.src: Some was because they didn't want to stand out.
segments.tr: Sebagian lagi karena mereka tidak ingin terlihat berbeda.

segments.src: Psychologists call these two motives:
segments.tr: Psikolog menyebut dua motif ini:

segments.src: - **Informational influence**: "They probably know better."
segments.tr: - **Pengaruh informasional**: “Mereka mungkin lebih tahu.”

segments.src: - **Normative influence**: "I want to fit in."
segments.tr: - **Pengaruh normatif**: “Saya ingin diterima.”

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Dalam Kehidupan Sehari-hari

segments.src: You're on Amazon looking for a $30 pair of wireless earbuds.
segments.tr: Anda sedang mencari earbuds nirkabel seharga $30 di Amazon.

segments.src: Two options look almost the same:
segments.tr: Dua pilihan terlihat hampir sama:

segments.src: - **Option A**: 4.4 stars, 12,000+ ratings, a "#1 Best Seller" badge, and "2K+ bought in past month"
segments.tr: - **Opsi A**: 4,4 bintang, lebih dari 12.000 rating, lencana “#1 Best Seller”, dan “2K+ dibeli dalam sebulan terakhir”

segments.src: - **Option B**: 4.6 stars, 38 ratings
segments.tr: - **Opsi B**: 4,6 bintang, 38 rating

segments.src: On paper, B is rated higher, yet many shoppers pick A anyway.
segments.tr: Di atas kertas, B mendapat rating lebih tinggi, namun banyak pembeli tetap memilih A.

segments.src: Each part of the listing is doing a different job:
segments.tr: Setiap bagian dari listing itu punya fungsi yang berbeda:

segments.src: - **Social proof:** The rating count and the "bought in past month" line tell you that lots of people chose A. When you can't test earbuds yourself, volume feels safer than a slightly higher average from a few people.
segments.tr: - **Bukti sosial:** Jumlah rating dan keterangan “dibeli dalam sebulan terakhir” menunjukkan bahwa banyak orang memilih A. Ketika Anda tidak bisa mencoba earbuds sendiri, jumlah yang besar terasa lebih aman dibanding rata-rata yang sedikit lebih tinggi dari segelintir orang.

segments.src: - **Word of mouth:** You scroll to reviews from people "like you," such as "Great for the gym" or "I use these on my commute on the subway." Similar reviewers carry extra weight.
segments.tr: - **Word of mouth:** Anda menggulir ke ulasan dari orang-orang “seperti Anda”, misalnya “Bagus untuk gym” atau “Saya memakainya saat naik kereta ke kantor”. Ulasan dari pengulas yang mirip punya bobot ekstra.

segments.src: - **Reference groups:** If your coworkers all wear AirPods, you might pay $100 more just to match them. Earbuds are visible, so they say something about you.
segments.tr: - **Kelompok referensi:** Jika rekan kerja Anda semua memakai AirPods, Anda mungkin rela membayar $100 lebih mahal hanya untuk menyamai mereka. Earbuds itu terlihat, jadi ia mengatakan sesuatu tentang diri Anda.

segments.src: Businesses use the same levers on purpose: "Most popular" plan labels on SaaS pricing pages, "Join 50,000 marketers" on newsletter sign-ups, and customer logos on B2B websites.
segments.tr: Bisnis dengan sengaja memakai taktik yang sama: label paket “Paling Populer” di halaman harga SaaS, “Bergabung bersama 50.000 marketer” pada pendaftaran newsletter, dan logo pelanggan di situs B2B.

segments.src: A well-known hotel study found that a card saying *most guests here reuse their towels* got more people to reuse towels than a card about saving the environment.
segments.tr: Sebuah studi hotel yang terkenal menemukan bahwa kartu bertuliskan *sebagian besar tamu di sini menggunakan ulang handuk mereka* membuat lebih banyak orang menggunakan ulang handuk dibanding kartu tentang menyelamatkan lingkungan.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Istilah Hari Ini

segments.src: - **Reference group**: Any group a person uses as a standard for their own attitudes and purchases.
segments.tr: - **Kelompok referensi**: Kelompok apa pun yang dijadikan standar oleh seseorang untuk sikap dan pembeliannya.

segments.src: - **Aspirational group**: A group you don't belong to yet but would like to join or resemble.
segments.tr: - **Kelompok aspirasi**: Kelompok yang belum Anda ikuti, tetapi ingin Anda masuki atau tiru.

segments.src: - **Word of mouth (WOM)**: Consumers sharing information and opinions about products with each other, offline or online.
segments.tr: - **Word of mouth (WOM)**: Konsumen berbagi informasi dan opini tentang produk satu sama lain, secara langsung maupun daring.

segments.src: - **Social proof**: The tendency to treat other people's behavior as evidence of the right choice, especially when we're unsure.
segments.tr: - **Bukti sosial**: Kecenderungan menganggap perilaku orang lain sebagai bukti pilihan yang benar, terutama ketika kita tidak yakin.

segments.src: - **Normative vs. informational influence**: Going along to fit in vs. going along because you think others know better.
segments.tr: - **Pengaruh normatif vs. informasional**: Mengikuti agar diterima vs. mengikuti karena menganggap orang lain lebih tahu.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今日の概念

segments.src: Picture two taco trucks parked side by side.
segments.tr: 並んで停まっている2台のタコストラックを想像してみてください。

segments.src: One has a line of 15 people.
segments.tr: 一方には15人の列ができています。

segments.src: The other has nobody.
segments.tr: もう一方には誰もいません。

segments.src: Most of us join the line, even though it means waiting longer.
segments.tr: 待ち時間が長くなると分かっていても、多くの人は列に並びます。

segments.src: We don't know anything about the food yet, but other people's choices feel like information.
segments.tr: 料理についてはまだ何も分からなくても、他人の選択は情報のように感じられるのです。

segments.src: That is **social influence**: our buying decisions change because of what other people do, say, or think.
segments.tr: それが**社会的影響**です。つまり、他人が何をし、何を言い、何を考えるかによって、私たちの購買決定は変わります。

segments.src: Consumer psychologists usually split it into three connected ideas.
segments.tr: 消費者心理学では、これを通常3つの関連する概念に分けて考えます。

segments.src: Reference groups.** These are the groups we use as a yardstick for our own choices.
segments.tr: 参照集団。** 自分の選択の物差しとして使う集団のことです。

segments.src: They come in a few types:
segments.tr: これにはいくつかの種類があります:

segments.src: - **Membership groups**: groups you already belong to, like your coworkers, your family, or your running club.
segments.tr: - **所属集団**: 同僚、家族、ランニング・クラブなど、すでに属している集団。

segments.src: - **Aspirational groups**: groups you'd like to belong to, like the senior engineers you hope to join or athletes you look up to.
segments.tr: - **憧れの集団**: 将来入りたいと願うシニアエンジニアの集団や、尊敬するアスリートなど、所属したいと思う集団。

segments.src: - **Dissociative groups**: groups you *don't* want to be associated with. People sometimes avoid a brand because "that's not who I am."
segments.tr: - **非所属集団（拒否集団）**: *関わりたくない*集団。「自分らしくないから」という理由でブランドを避けることがあります。

segments.src: Reference groups matter most for products other people can see, like sneakers, cars, phones, and the bag you carry to work.
segments.tr: 参照集団が最も重要になるのは、スニーカー、車、スマートフォン、通勤に持っていくバッグなど、他人の目に触れる製品です。

segments.src: They matter much less for things nobody notices, like your brand of dish soap.
segments.tr: 食器用洗剤のように誰も気に留めないものでは、影響はずっと小さくなります。

segments.src: Word of mouth (WOM).** This means consumers telling other consumers about products.
segments.tr: 口コミ（WOM）。** 消費者同士が製品について語り合うことを指します。

segments.src: Today that includes a friend's text ("you have to try this"), a TikTok review, and a Reddit thread.
segments.tr: 今日では、友人からのメッセージ（「これ絶対試して！」）、TikTokのレビュー、Redditのスレッドなどがこれに当たります。

segments.src: People tend to trust WOM more than ads because the speaker doesn't seem to be trying to sell anything.
segments.tr: 話し手が何かを売ろうとしているようには見えないため、人々は広告よりも口コミを信頼する傾向があります。

segments.src: That trust is also why undisclosed paid endorsements are a problem.
segments.tr: その信頼こそが、開示されていない有料の推薦が問題になる理由でもあります。

segments.src: The U.S.
segments.tr: 米国の

segments.src: Federal Trade Commission requires influencers to disclose material connections to brands.
segments.tr: 連邦取引委員会（FTC）は、インフルエンサーにブランドとの重要な関係を開示することを求めています。

segments.src: Social proof.** This term was popularized by psychologist Robert Cialdini.
segments.tr: 社会的証明。** この用語は心理学者ロバート・チャルディーニによって広められました。

segments.src: When we're unsure what to do, we look at what others are doing and assume they know something.
segments.tr: 何をすべきか分からないとき、人は他人が何をしているかを見て、彼らが何かを知っているのだろうと考えます。

segments.src: Uncertainty makes the effect stronger, and so does similarity: the more the "others" resemble us, the more their choices count.
segments.tr: 不確実性が高いほどこの効果は強まり、また「他者」が自分と似ているほど、その人たちの選択が重みを持ちます。

segments.src: Classic research shows how strong this pull is.
segments.tr: 古典的な研究は、この引力の強さを示しています。

segments.src: In Solomon Asch's 1950s line-judgment experiments, many participants went along at least once with a group answer that was plainly wrong.
segments.tr: ソロモン・アッシュの1950年代の線分判断実験では、明らかに間違っている集団の答えに、少なくとも一度は同調した参加者が多くいました。

segments.src: Some of that was because they doubted their own eyes.
segments.tr: その一部は、自分の目を疑ったためでした。

segments.src: Some was because they didn't want to stand out.
segments.tr: また一部は、目立つことを避けたかったからでした。

segments.src: Psychologists call these two motives:
segments.tr: 心理学者はこの2つの動機を次のように呼びます:

segments.src: - **Informational influence**: "They probably know better."
segments.tr: - **情報的影響**: 「彼らの方が詳しいのだろう。」

segments.src: - **Normative influence**: "I want to fit in."
segments.tr: - **規範的影響**: 「周りに馴染みたい。」

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 日常生活では

segments.src: You're on Amazon looking for a $30 pair of wireless earbuds.
segments.tr: Amazonで30ドルのワイヤレスイヤホンを探しているとします。

segments.src: Two options look almost the same:
segments.tr: ほとんど同じに見える選択肢が2つあります:

segments.src: - **Option A**: 4.4 stars, 12,000+ ratings, a "#1 Best Seller" badge, and "2K+ bought in past month"
segments.tr: - **選択肢A**: 4.4つ星、12,000件以上の評価、「#1 Best Seller」バッジ、「過去1か月で2K+購入」

segments.src: - **Option B**: 4.6 stars, 38 ratings
segments.tr: - **選択肢B**: 4.6つ星、38件の評価

segments.src: On paper, B is rated higher, yet many shoppers pick A anyway.
segments.tr: 数字だけ見ればBの評価は高いのに、多くの買い物客は結局Aを選びます。

segments.src: Each part of the listing is doing a different job:
segments.tr: 商品ページの各部分は、それぞれ異なる役割を果たしています:

segments.src: - **Social proof:** The rating count and the "bought in past month" line tell you that lots of people chose A. When you can't test earbuds yourself, volume feels safer than a slightly higher average from a few people.
segments.tr: - **社会的証明:** 評価件数と「過去1か月で購入」の表示は、多くの人がAを選んだことを示しています。イヤホンを自分で試せないとき、少数の人による少し高い平均点より、件数の多さの方が安心に感じられます。

segments.src: - **Word of mouth:** You scroll to reviews from people "like you," such as "Great for the gym" or "I use these on my commute on the subway." Similar reviewers carry extra weight.
segments.tr: - **口コミ:** 「ジムで最高」や「地下鉄での通勤で使っています」など、「自分に似た」レビュアーのレビューを読みます。似たレビュアーの言葉は、より大きな重みを持ちます。

segments.src: - **Reference groups:** If your coworkers all wear AirPods, you might pay $100 more just to match them. Earbuds are visible, so they say something about you.
segments.tr: - **参照集団:** 同僚全員がAirPodsを使っているなら、周りに合わせるためだけに100ドル余計に払うかもしれません。イヤホンは目に見えるので、その人について何かを語ってしまうのです。

segments.src: Businesses use the same levers on purpose: "Most popular" plan labels on SaaS pricing pages, "Join 50,000 marketers" on newsletter sign-ups, and customer logos on B2B websites.
segments.tr: 企業も意図的に同じ仕掛けを使います。SaaSの料金ページにある「最も人気」のプランラベル、ニュースレター登録の「5万人のマーケターが参加」、B2Bサイトの顧客ロゴなどです。

segments.src: A well-known hotel study found that a card saying *most guests here reuse their towels* got more people to reuse towels than a card about saving the environment.
segments.tr: 有名なホテルの研究では、「*ここに泊まったお客様の多くがタオルを再利用しています*」というカードの方が、環境保護を訴えるカードよりもタオルの再利用を促した、という結果が出ています。

de.title: [Consumer Psychology #13] Warum „4,000 Leute haben das gekauft“ auf uns wirkt (auch wenn wir wissen, dass es nicht sollte)

segments.src: > We rarely shop alone: the people we belong to, the people we admire, and even total strangers' reviews quietly shape what we buy.
segments.tr: > Wir kaufen selten allein: Die Gruppen, zu denen wir gehören, die Menschen, die wir bewundern, und sogar die Bewertungen völlig fremder Menschen beeinflussen still und leise, was wir kaufen.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Heutiges Konzept

segments.src: Picture two taco trucks parked side by side.
segments.tr: Stell dir zwei Taco-Trucks vor, die nebeneinander stehen.

segments.src: One has a line of 15 people.
segments.tr: Der eine hat eine Schlange von 15 Leuten.

segments.src: The other has nobody.
segments.tr: Beim anderen steht niemand an.

segments.src: Most of us join the line, even though it means waiting longer.
segments.tr: Die meisten von uns stellen sich an, obwohl das längeres Warten bedeutet.

segments.src: We don't know anything about the food yet, but other people's choices feel like information.
segments.tr: Wir wissen über das Essen noch gar nichts, aber die Entscheidungen anderer fühlen sich wie eine Information an.

segments.src: That is **social influence**: our buying decisions change because of what other people do, say, or think.
segments.tr: Das ist **soziale Beeinflussung**: Unsere Kaufentscheidungen ändern sich wegen dessen, was andere Menschen tun, sagen oder denken.

segments.src: Consumer psychologists usually split it into three connected ideas.
segments.tr: Konsumpsychologen unterteilen das meist in drei zusammenhängende Konzepte.

segments.src: Reference groups.** These are the groups we use as a yardstick for our own choices.
segments.tr: Bezugsgruppen.** Das sind die Gruppen, an denen wir unsere eigenen Entscheidungen messen.

segments.src: They come in a few types:
segments.tr: Es gibt davon einige Arten:

segments.src: - **Membership groups**: groups you already belong to, like your coworkers, your family, or your running club.
segments.tr: - **Zugehörigkeitsgruppen**: Gruppen, denen du bereits angehörst, etwa deine Kolleg:innen, deine Familie oder dein Laufclub.

segments.src: - **Aspirational groups**: groups you'd like to belong to, like the senior engineers you hope to join or athletes you look up to.
segments.tr: - **Wunschgruppen**: Gruppen, denen du gern angehören würdest, etwa die Senior-Entwickler, denen du beitreten möchtest, oder Sportler, zu denen du aufschaust.

segments.src: - **Dissociative groups**: groups you *don't* want to be associated with. People sometimes avoid a brand because "that's not who I am."
segments.tr: - **Abgrenzungsgruppen**: Gruppen, mit denen du *nicht* in Verbindung gebracht werden willst. Manche Menschen meiden eine Marke mit der Begründung „das bin ich nicht“.

segments.src: Reference groups matter most for products other people can see, like sneakers, cars, phones, and the bag you carry to work.
segments.tr: Bezugsgruppen sind vor allem bei Produkten wichtig, die andere sehen können, etwa Sneaker, Autos, Handys und die Tasche, die man zur Arbeit trägt.

segments.src: They matter much less for things nobody notices, like your brand of dish soap.
segments.tr: Bei Dingen, die niemandem auffallen, etwa deiner Spülmittelmarke, spielen sie eine viel geringere Rolle.

segments.src: Word of mouth (WOM).** This means consumers telling other consumers about products.
segments.tr: Mundpropaganda (WOM).** Gemeint ist, dass Verbraucher anderen Verbrauchern von Produkten erzählen.

segments.src: Today that includes a friend's text ("you have to try this"), a TikTok review, and a Reddit thread.
segments.tr: Heute gehören dazu die Nachricht einer Freundin („Das musst du unbedingt probieren“), eine TikTok-Bewertung und ein Reddit-Thread.

segments.src: People tend to trust WOM more than ads because the speaker doesn't seem to be trying to sell anything.
segments.tr: Menschen vertrauen Mundpropaganda oft mehr als Werbung, weil der Sprechende nicht so wirkt, als wolle er etwas verkaufen.

segments.src: That trust is also why undisclosed paid endorsements are a problem.
segments.tr: Genau dieses Vertrauen macht nicht offengelegte bezahlte Empfehlungen zum Problem.

segments.src: The U.S.
segments.tr: Die U.S.

segments.src: Federal Trade Commission requires influencers to disclose material connections to brands.
segments.tr: Federal Trade Commission verlangt, dass Influencer wesentliche Verbindungen zu Marken offenlegen.

segments.src: Social proof.** This term was popularized by psychologist Robert Cialdini.
segments.tr: Sozialer Beweis.** Dieser Begriff wurde vom Psychologen Robert Cialdini bekannt gemacht.

segments.src: When we're unsure what to do, we look at what others are doing and assume they know something.
segments.tr: Wenn wir unsicher sind, was wir tun sollen, sehen wir, was andere tun, und nehmen an, dass sie etwas wissen.

segments.src: Uncertainty makes the effect stronger, and so does similarity: the more the "others" resemble us, the more their choices count.
segments.tr: Unsicherheit verstärkt den Effekt, ebenso Ähnlichkeit: Je mehr die „Anderen“ uns gleichen, desto mehr zählt ihre Entscheidung.

segments.src: Classic research shows how strong this pull is.
segments.tr: Klassische Forschung zeigt, wie stark dieser Sog ist.

segments.src: In Solomon Asch's 1950s line-judgment experiments, many participants went along at least once with a group answer that was plainly wrong.
segments.tr: In Solomon Aschs Linienvergleichs-Experimenten aus den 1950er-Jahren schlossen sich viele Teilnehmende mindestens einmal einer Gruppenantwort an, die offensichtlich falsch war.

segments.src: Some of that was because they doubted their own eyes.
segments.tr: Teilweise lag das daran, dass sie ihren eigenen Augen nicht trauten.

segments.src: Some was because they didn't want to stand out.
segments.tr: Teilweise wollten sie nicht auffallen.

segments.src: Psychologists call these two motives:
segments.tr: Psychologen nennen diese beiden Motive:

segments.src: - **Informational influence**: "They probably know better."
segments.tr: - **Informationelle Beeinflussung**: „Die wissen wahrscheinlich besser Bescheid.“

segments.src: - **Normative influence**: "I want to fit in."
segments.tr: - **Normative Beeinflussung**: „Ich will dazugehören.“

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Im Alltag

segments.src: You're on Amazon looking for a $30 pair of wireless earbuds.
segments.tr: Du suchst bei Amazon nach einem Paar kabelloser Ohrhörer für 30 $.

segments.src: Two options look almost the same:
segments.tr: Zwei Optionen sehen fast gleich aus:

segments.src: - **Option A**: 4.4 stars, 12,000+ ratings, a "#1 Best Seller" badge, and "2K+ bought in past month"
segments.tr: - **Option A**: 4.4 Sterne, 12,000+ Bewertungen, ein Badge „#1 Bestseller“ und „2K+ im letzten Monat gekauft“

segments.src: - **Option B**: 4.6 stars, 38 ratings
segments.tr: - **Option B**: 4.6 Sterne, 38 Bewertungen

segments.src: On paper, B is rated higher, yet many shoppers pick A anyway.
segments.tr: Auf dem Papier ist B besser bewertet, trotzdem entscheiden sich viele Käufer für A.

segments.src: Each part of the listing is doing a different job:
segments.tr: Jeder Teil des Angebots erfüllt eine andere Aufgabe:

segments.src: - **Social proof:** The rating count and the "bought in past month" line tell you that lots of people chose A. When you can't test earbuds yourself, volume feels safer than a slightly higher average from a few people.
segments.tr: - **Sozialer Beweis:** Die Anzahl der Bewertungen und die Angabe „im letzten Monat gekauft“ zeigen dir, dass sich viele Menschen für A entschieden haben. Wenn du Ohrhörer nicht selbst testen kannst, wirkt Masse sicherer als ein etwas höherer Durchschnitt von wenigen Stimmen.

segments.src: - **Word of mouth:** You scroll to reviews from people "like you," such as "Great for the gym" or "I use these on my commute on the subway." Similar reviewers carry extra weight.
segments.tr: - **Mundpropaganda:** Du scrollst zu Bewertungen von Leuten, die dir „ähnlich“ sind, etwa „Super fürs Fitnessstudio“ oder „Ich benutze die auf dem Weg zur Arbeit in der U-Bahn“. Ähnliche Rezensenten haben mehr Gewicht.

segments.src: - **Reference groups:** If your coworkers all wear AirPods, you might pay $100 more just to match them. Earbuds are visible, so they say something about you.
segments.tr: - **Bezugsgruppen:** Wenn deine Kolleg:innen alle AirPods tragen, zahlst du vielleicht 100 $ mehr, nur um mitzuhalten. Ohrhörer sind sichtbar und sagen etwas über dich aus.

segments.src: Businesses use the same levers on purpose: "Most popular" plan labels on SaaS pricing pages, "Join 50,000 marketers" on newsletter sign-ups, and customer logos on B2B websites.
segments.tr: Unternehmen nutzen dieselben Hebel bewusst: „Beliebteste“-Tarifbezeichnungen auf SaaS-Preisseiten, „Schließ dich 50,000 Marketern an“ bei Newsletter-Anmeldungen und Kundenlogos auf B2B-Websites.

segments.src: A well-known hotel study found that a card saying *most guests here reuse their towels* got more people to reuse towels than a card about saving the environment.
segments.tr: Eine bekannte Hotelstudie ergab, dass ein Hinweis mit dem Satz *die meisten Gäste hier verwenden ihre Handtücher erneut* mehr Menschen dazu brachte, Handtücher wiederzuverwenden, als ein Hinweis zum Umweltschutz.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Zusammenfassung in 3 Zeilen

segments.src: 1. Reference groups (the ones you belong to, want to join, or want to avoid) shape choices most strongly for products that other people can see.
segments.tr: 1. Bezugsgruppen (denen man angehört, denen man beitreten möchte oder die man meiden will) prägen Entscheidungen am stärksten bei Produkten, die andere sehen können.

segments.src: 2. Word of mouth is persuasive because it seems independent of the seller. That makes honesty and disclosure important.
segments.tr: 2. Mundpropaganda überzeugt, weil sie unabhängig vom Verkäufer wirkt. Deshalb sind Ehrlichkeit und Offenlegung wichtig.

segments.src: 3. Social proof is strongest when we feel uncertain and when the "others" seem similar to us. It works through both "they know better" and "I want to fit in."
segments.tr: 3. Sozialer Beweis wirkt am stärksten, wenn wir unsicher sind und die „Anderen“ uns ähnlich erscheinen. Er wirkt sowohl über „Die wissen es besser“ als auch über „Ich will dazugehören“.

segments.src: Classic research shows how strong this pull is.
segments.tr: Nghiên cứu kinh điển cho thấy sức hút này mạnh đến mức nào.

segments.src: In Solomon Asch's 1950s line-judgment experiments, many participants went along at least once with a group answer that was plainly wrong.
segments.tr: Trong các thí nghiệm đánh giá độ dài đường thẳng của Solomon Asch vào những năm 1950, nhiều người tham gia đã làm theo câu trả lời tập thể rõ ràng là sai ít nhất một lần.

segments.src: Some of that was because they doubted their own eyes.
segments.tr: Một phần là do họ nghi ngờ chính đôi mắt của mình.

segments.src: Some was because they didn't want to stand out.
segments.tr: Một phần là vì họ không muốn nổi bật.

segments.src: Psychologists call these two motives:
segments.tr: Các nhà tâm lý học gọi đây là hai động cơ:

segments.src: - **Informational influence**: "They probably know better."
segments.tr: - **Ảnh hưởng mang tính thông tin**: "Có lẽ họ biết rõ hơn."

segments.src: - **Normative influence**: "I want to fit in."
segments.tr: - **Ảnh hưởng mang tính chuẩn mực**: "Tôi muốn hòa nhập."

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Trong đời sống hằng ngày

segments.src: You're on Amazon looking for a $30 pair of wireless earbuds.
segments.tr: Bạn đang tìm trên Amazon một đôi tai nghe không dây giá 30 USD.

segments.src: Two options look almost the same:
segments.tr: Hai lựa chọn trông gần như giống hệt nhau:

segments.src: - **Option A**: 4.4 stars, 12,000+ ratings, a "#1 Best Seller" badge, and "2K+ bought in past month"
segments.tr: - **Lựa chọn A**: 4,4 sao, hơn 12.000 lượt đánh giá, huy hiệu "#1 Best Seller" và "2K+ đã mua trong tháng qua"

segments.src: - **Option B**: 4.6 stars, 38 ratings
segments.tr: - **Lựa chọn B**: 4,6 sao, 38 lượt đánh giá

segments.src: On paper, B is rated higher, yet many shoppers pick A anyway.
segments.tr: Trên giấy tờ, B được đánh giá cao hơn, nhưng nhiều người mua vẫn chọn A.

segments.src: Each part of the listing is doing a different job:
segments.tr: Mỗi phần của trang sản phẩm đảm nhiệm một vai trò khác nhau:

segments.src: - **Social proof:** The rating count and the "bought in past month" line tell you that lots of people chose A. When you can't test earbuds yourself, volume feels safer than a slightly higher average from a few people.
segments.tr: - **Bằng chứng xã hội:** Số lượt đánh giá và dòng "đã mua trong tháng qua" cho bạn biết rất nhiều người đã chọn A. Khi bạn không thể tự thử tai nghe, số lượng lớn mang lại cảm giác an toàn hơn so với mức điểm trung bình cao hơn một chút từ vài người.

segments.src: - **Word of mouth:** You scroll to reviews from people "like you," such as "Great for the gym" or "I use these on my commute on the subway." Similar reviewers carry extra weight.
segments.tr: - **Truyền miệng:** Bạn cuộn xuống các đánh giá từ những người "giống bạn", chẳng hạn "Tuyệt vời khi tập gym" hoặc "Tôi dùng chúng khi đi làm bằng tàu điện ngầm". Những người đánh giá tương đồng có sức nặng lớn hơn.

segments.src: - **Reference groups:** If your coworkers all wear AirPods, you might pay $100 more just to match them. Earbuds are visible, so they say something about you.
segments.tr: - **Nhóm tham chiếu:** Nếu đồng nghiệp của bạn đều dùng AirPods, bạn có thể sẵn sàng trả thêm 100 USD chỉ để giống họ. Tai nghe là thứ nhìn thấy được, nên chúng nói lên điều gì đó về bạn.

segments.src: Businesses use the same levers on purpose: "Most popular" plan labels on SaaS pricing pages, "Join 50,000 marketers" on newsletter sign-ups, and customer logos on B2B websites.
segments.tr: Các doanh nghiệp cố ý sử dụng chính những đòn bẩy này: nhãn "Phổ biến nhất" trên trang giá dịch vụ SaaS, "Tham gia cùng 50.000 nhà tiếp thị" khi đăng ký bản tin, và logo khách hàng trên các trang web B2B.

segments.src: A well-known hotel study found that a card saying *most guests here reuse their towels* got more people to reuse towels than a card about saving the environment.
segments.tr: Một nghiên cứu khách sạn nổi tiếng cho thấy tấm thẻ ghi *phần lớn khách ở đây đều tái sử dụng khăn tắm* khiến nhiều người tái sử dụng khăn hơn so với tấm thẻ kêu gọi bảo vệ môi trường.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Tóm tắt trong 3 dòng

segments.src: 1. Reference groups (the ones you belong to, want to join, or want to avoid) shape choices most strongly for products that other people can see.
segments.tr: 1. Nhóm tham chiếu (nhóm ta thuộc về, muốn gia nhập hoặc muốn tránh) định hình lựa chọn mạnh nhất đối với những sản phẩm mà người khác có thể nhìn thấy.

segments.src: 2. Word of mouth is persuasive because it seems independent of the seller. That makes honesty and disclosure important.
segments.tr: 2. Truyền miệng có sức thuyết phục vì nó dường như độc lập với người bán. Vì vậy, tính trung thực và việc công khai thông tin là rất quan trọng.

segments.src: 3. Social proof is strongest when we feel uncertain and when the "others" seem similar to us. It works through both "they know better" and "I want to fit in."
segments.tr: 3. Bằng chứng xã hội mạnh nhất khi ta cảm thấy bất định và khi "những người khác" có vẻ giống ta. Nó tác động qua cả "họ biết rõ hơn" lẫn "tôi muốn hòa nhập".

segments.tr: Nó chủ yếu sử dụng nguyên tắc nào?

segments.src: - (a) Social proof
segments.tr: - (a) Bằng chứng xã hội

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Thuật ngữ hôm nay

segments.src: - **Reference group**: Any group a person uses as a standard for their own attitudes and purchases.
segments.tr: - **Nhóm tham chiếu**: Bất kỳ nhóm nào mà một người dùng làm chuẩn mực cho thái độ và việc mua sắm của chính mình.

segments.src: - **Aspirational group**: A group you don't belong to yet but would like to join or resemble.
segments.tr: - **Nhóm khát vọng**: Nhóm mà bạn chưa thuộc về nhưng muốn gia nhập hoặc giống như vậy.

segments.src: - **Word of mouth (WOM)**: Consumers sharing information and opinions about products with each other, offline or online.
segments.tr: - **Truyền miệng (WOM)**: Người tiêu dùng chia sẻ thông tin và ý kiến về sản phẩm với nhau, trực tiếp hoặc trực tuyến.

segments.src: - **Social proof**: The tendency to treat other people's behavior as evidence of the right choice, especially when we're unsure.
segments.tr: - **Bằng chứng xã hội**: Xu hướng coi hành vi của người khác là bằng chứng cho lựa chọn đúng đắn, đặc biệt khi ta không chắc chắn.

segments.src: - **Normative vs. informational influence**: Going along to fit in vs. going along because you think others know better.
segments.tr: - **Ảnh hưởng chuẩn mực so với ảnh hưởng thông tin**: Làm theo để hòa nhập so với làm theo vì nghĩ rằng người khác biết rõ hơn.

segments.src: *Answers: Q1 is (c).
segments.tr: *Đáp án: Q1 là (c).

segments.src: The student is steering away from a group they don't want to be identified with.
segments.tr: Sinh viên đang tránh xa một nhóm mà họ không muốn bị nhận diện là thành viên.

segments.src: Q2 is False.
segments.tr: Q2 là Sai.

segments.src: Social proof works best when people feel **uncertain**; confident shoppers rely more on their own judgment.
segments.tr: Bằng chứng xã hội hoạt động hiệu quả nhất khi người ta cảm thấy **bất định**; người mua tự tin hơn sẽ dựa nhiều hơn vào phán đoán của chính họ.

segments.src: Q3 is (a).
segments.tr: Q3 là (a).

segments.src: "Most Popular" tells visitors what others chose and suggests that choosing it is safe and normal.
segments.tr: "Phổ biến nhất" cho khách truy cập biết người khác đã chọn gì và gợi ý rằng việc chọn nó là an toàn và bình thường.
